title: Zero-Sum Game
body_html:
Zero-Sum Game

A zero-sum game in strategic form is a triple $(I,J,g)$ where $I$ is the nonempty strategy set of the maximizing player, $J$ is the nonempty strategy set of the minimizing player, and $g : I \times J \to \mathbb{R}$ is the payoff of the maximizing player. If the chosen strategies are $(i,j)$, then the maximizing player receives $g(i,j)$ and the minimizing player receives $-g(i,j)$.

References

  • [MFoGT, Def. 2.2.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MechDesign.pdf. Zero-sum strategic-form game as a triple (I,J,g).
